title: World Kangaroo Day: How climate change impacts Australia’s macropods
summary: For World Kangaroo Day, Mongabay looks at how a hotter, drier Australia is putting pressure on its 59 species of kangaroos, wallabies and their smaller relatives. Long droughts and bushfires have killed or driven off millions of the big kangaroos in bad years. Small, rare species such as Gilbert's potoroo and the mala could be pushed toward extinction. A record-breaking 'super El Niño' is expected to bring more heat and fire, so scientists are calling for Indigenous-led fire management, restored waterways and protected cool refuges.
caption: A mother kangaroo waits for kinder rains
alt: A watercolor of a worried eastern grey kangaroo with a joey peeking from her pouch, sitting by a dried-up waterhole under a hazy dusk sky, with a gum tree, a tiny hare-wallaby hiding in a shrub, fading footprints and a distant smoky glow.

title: This spider catapults ants
summary: Scientists in Australia have found a new kind of ballista spider with a very unusual way of hunting. Instead of chasing its food, it pulls its silk web tight like a spring, and the web seems to be built for just one prey: the feisty green tree ant. Researchers think the spider may even get the ants to attack the trap, so the ants set off the catapult themselves. No other spider is known to build a web for a single prey species, or one that the prey sets off.
caption: A tiny spider with a spring-loaded silk surprise
alt: A watercolor of a round-eyed, rosy-cheeked tan spider hanging in warm Australian forest light. It holds a tight silk line pulled back from a cone-shaped web while green tree ants creep along the web, a gum branch and a leafy ant nest.

title: Rare Indonesian maleo birds face new threat from international exotic pet trade
summary: Researchers have recorded the first known cases of critically endangered maleos being smuggled abroad: in 2024, 25 young birds from Sulawesi were seized on their way to, or after arriving in, India's exotic pet market. All of them were juveniles, so scientists think the chicks were taken from hatcheries meant to protect the species. They are asking for tighter airport checks, a crackdown on corruption and a way to send rescued birds home.
caption: A lone maleo waits by an empty nest
alt: A watercolor of a sad-eyed black-and-pink maleo with a dark helmet-like casque standing on a dusky Sulawesi beach beside an empty, dug-out egg pit, with tiny footprints fading away, a hatchery fence and a faraway plane in the sky.

title: Six beluga deaths cast a shadow over rescue from Canada’s Marineland
summary: This summer, 30 belugas were moved from Canada's closed Marineland park to aquariums in the U.S. and Spain. Six of them have died in the two months since. Exams found long-lasting illnesses, which experts link to years of poor care. The other belugas are eating and settling in, and advocates are pushing harder to stop keeping whales and dolphins in captivity.
caption: Six little bubbles drift toward the light
alt: A soft watercolor of a gentle white beluga with a tiny tear, floating in dusky blue-violet water as six fading bubbles rise toward the evening surface, while two pale belugas swim in the distance above seagrass and pebbles.

title: In Nepal, AI builds on local knowledge to help prevent tiger attacks
summary: In Nepal's Bardiya region, which now has more tigers than ever before, researchers tried out cheap solar-powered listening boxes. The boxes picked up chital deer alarm calls and mapped where a tiger or leopard might be lurking, so villagers could keep clear. Forest guards said the alerts matched what they saw on the ground, but the pilot ran out of money and staff, so the devices were moved to India instead of being expanded.
caption: When the deer call, the forest listens
alt: A watercolor of a round-faced tiger sitting calmly in golden Terai grass while a spotted chital deer calls out nearby, a rhesus monkey watches from a branch, and a small solar listening box hangs on a tree trunk.

title: Funding uncertainty threatens Tasmania’s gains against kelp-grazing sea urchins
summary: As Tasmania's waters have warmed, long-spined sea urchins have spread south and have been eating away the kelp forests there. The state pays divers extra to harvest the urchins for their roe, and this has helped kelp grow back in some places. Scientists warn that the money is now only promised one year at a time, so that progress could be lost.
caption: A prickly guest, and kelp trying to return
alt: A watercolor of a round purple sea urchin with long spines and big shiny eyes, sitting on the Tasmanian seafloor between golden kelp on one side and bare pink rock on the other, with a rock lobster, an abalone shell and a diver's bubbles nearby.

title: Celebrity shark trapped in South Korean canal stirs concerns over warming seas
summary: Bukangi is a 3-meter female dusky shark, an endangered species. Since mid-September she has been stuck in a shallow canal in Busan's North Port Waterfront Park, where about 1.4 million people have come to see her and the city has named her an honorary ambassador. Two attempts to guide her out to sea have failed so far. Some people see her arrival as a sign of warming seas, but scientists say one shark isn't enough to prove that.
caption: Bukangi dreams of the open sea
alt: A watercolor of a round-faced, wide-eyed dusky shark wearing a small gold rosette, swimming in a stone-walled city canal under sunlit water, with yellowtail fish, seaweed and pebbles around her, and skyscrapers, a ferry and a row of spectators at a railing above the surface.

title: As US states reduce recently restored wolf populations, here’s what we risk losing (commentary)
summary: Two filmmakers spent six years living beside a gray wolf pack in Idaho. They saw the wolves raise pups, look after injured packmates and grieve the ones they lost. They warn that Idaho, Wyoming and Montana are now pushing hard to cut their recently restored wolf numbers, and that breaking up these families takes away the elders who teach the young. They argue for nonlethal ways for people and wolves to share the land.
caption: A small pack, holding close at dusk
alt: A watercolor of a gray wolf with droopy ears and a single tear, sitting beside a sleeping pup in front of an empty den, below the jagged Sawtooth Mountains at dusk, while faint paw prints fade away across the snow.

title: Vulture conservation project to target illegal killing and poisoning in Chad
summary: Vultures are disappearing from Chad. They are poisoned, sometimes by accident with baits set for jackals and leopards, and sometimes on purpose so their body parts can be sold for luck charms, and last year more than 100 Rüppell's vultures died that way. Sahara Conservation is starting a project in the Ouadi Rimé–Ouadi Achim reserve and around Lake Fitri to protect the endangered Egyptian vultures that spend the winter there. It will train wildlife officers, look into poisonings, and help herders protect their animals with fences and scare devices instead of poison.
caption: A watchful guardian waits by Lake Fitri
alt: A cute cream-white Egyptian vulture with a sunny yellow face and a shaggy crest sits on a rock at dusk above Lake Fitri. Behind it are an acacia tree with an empty nest, a low fence, far-off cattle and three vultures flying overhead, and a single feather drifts across the dry grass below.

title: Thailand seizes ivory shipment from Zambia, to launch DNA investigation
summary: Thai officials found about 400 pieces of African elephant ivory hidden inside logs in a timber shipment that was declared as coming from Zambia. Forensic experts will now test the ivory's DNA to work out where the elephants lived and to help Interpol track down the traffickers. Conservationists warn that big seizures like this one suggest the ivory trade hasn't really slowed down, and that keeps putting living elephants at risk.
caption: A little elephant remembers the ones who wandered away
alt: A watercolor of a small grey elephant calf with droopy ears and a single tear, standing by a misty river at dusk, with fading footprints, a wilted flower and a pile of cut logs in the foreground and a faraway herd on the horizon.

title: Two rare pregnancies spark hope for Sumatran rhinos — but also concerns about inbreeding
summary: Two critically endangered Sumatran rhinos at an Indonesian sanctuary are pregnant: Ratu, expecting her fourth calf, and her daughter Delilah, expecting her second, with both babies due around May 2027. It's welcome news for a species with only a few dozen animals left in the wild. It also shows how hard the breeding program's genetics are, though. All the males in the program are related, and Delilah's calf was fathered by her own uncle.
caption: Two little miracles on the way
alt: A watercolor of a fuzzy reddish-brown Sumatran rhino standing by a mud wallow in a sunny rainforest sanctuary, with a smaller rhino behind her, a nest with two eggs on a wooden fence, a heart-shaped leaf and butterflies.

title: ‘A hard reset’: Cape Town to capture and relocate baboon troops
summary: On the slopes of Table Mountain above Simon's Town, a 44-member troop of chacma baboons keeps coming down to raid a naval base and nearby homes for food, even with monitors trying to chase them off. Cape Town officials now plan to capture whole troops and move them somewhere else, which they're calling a hard reset of a long-running conflict between people and baboons.
caption: Cereal thief of Simon's Town, awaiting a new home
alt: A watercolor of a round-faced young chacma baboon sitting on a sunlit rock above Simon's Town. It holds a stolen bag of cereal, with red-brick barracks, a harbour, Table Mountain and more baboons walking down a ravine path behind it.

title: This is a South African cheetah, and it’s in trouble
summary: A huge census covering almost 100,000 square kilometers of South Africa counted only 83 adult cheetahs living outside protected areas. Fences, farms and development are cutting off the routes these cats use to roam across borders and find mates, and some farmers kill them even though the survey found they hunt mostly wild prey. Researchers say the cheetah should be listed as endangered in South Africa.
caption: One of so few, watching the fences grow
alt: A watercolor of a spotted cheetah sitting alone at dusk on golden grassland beside a wire fence, a small tear on its cheek, with faint pawprints fading behind it and springbok far off on the horizon.

title: Deadly wildfires leave Borneo wildlife scrambling for fresh water
summary: An intense fire season in West Kalimantan, Indonesian Borneo, has dried up forest pools and turned village ponds salty, so thirsty monkeys and other wildlife are wandering toward homes and the coast to find water. A local conservation group found at least 16 dead animals between August and late September, among them proboscis monkeys, silvered langurs and long-tailed macaques. That is more than its patrols had recorded in almost six years. Villagers and conservationists are putting out water and rescuing animals that need help.

title: Sri Lanka elephant found with a gunshot wound. How can tuskers be protected?
summary: Kavantissa, one of Sri Lanka's tallest living tuskers, was found limping with a gunshot wound near a known human-elephant conflict zone. Wildlife vets sedated and treated him with antibiotics, and though he's recovering, he has grown more agitated and now faces renewed danger as he wanders between forest patches and villages. The story recalls a younger tusker companion who suffered a similar injury and later died.
caption: A gentle giant, wounded but walking on
alt: A soft watercolor painting at dusk of a gentle Sri Lankan tusker with long ivory tusks, drooping ears and a small tear, walking along a path between forest patches and a village where the lamps are lit, beside a trail of small footprints that fades away and a wilted flower.

title: Ethiopian highlands yield a new species of egg-eating snake
summary: Scientists discovered a brand-new snake species hiding in Ethiopia's misty Bale Mountains forests — a glossy black, nonvenomous snake with a bright white throat that eats only bird eggs, cracking them with special bones in its neck. Researchers named it the white-throated egg-eater after years of careful study confirmed it was unlike any known species. Sadly, locals often kill snakes out of fear, even though this gentle egg-eater poses no danger to people.
caption: A new black-and-white wonder of the forest
alt: A watercolor of a cute glossy black snake with a bright white throat and big shining eyes, coiled on the mossy floor of a misty Ethiopian highland forest and gazing at a nest of speckled bird eggs, with lichen-draped branches, a distant hut and blue mountains behind.

title: Arabian Sea humpbacks may be a unique subspecies at risk of extinction
summary: A new genetic study reveals that humpback whales living year-round in the Arabian Sea are likely their own distinct subspecies, isolated from other humpbacks for tens of thousands of years. This uniqueness comes with a cost: the population is small, has very low genetic diversity, and faces serious threats from fishing nets and ship traffic, making conservation efforts urgent.
caption: Alone in warm seas, waiting to be known
alt: A chubby, wide-eyed humpback whale floats alone at sunset in the warm Arabian Sea with one long pale flipper raised, while Oman's hazy cliffs, a far-off cargo ship, a small school of fish and a drifting orange fishing float sit around it.

title: ‘There could be local extinction’: The fight to protect Indonesia’s orangutans as El Niño fuels fires
summary: A fierce El Niño-driven fire season is tearing through Indonesian rainforests that shelter most of the world's critically endangered Bornean orangutans. Rescuers have already saved dozens of orangutans, some with severe burns, including a young one named Novita, while conservationists warn that mothers with babies are especially at risk because they tend to stay near their home trees even as flames close in.
caption: Through the smoke, a small orangutan waits for rescue
alt: A watercolor of a small, teary-eyed Bornean orangutan clinging to a vine on a branch while orange smoke hangs over the burned forest, and far off a rescuer's headlamp shines toward it.

title: Artificial nests give Hong Kong’s cockatoos a home – and a chance to study their behavior
summary: In busy Hong Kong, conservationists are climbing city trees to install cozy nest boxes for the critically endangered yellow-crested cockatoo. The city's feral flock, now the largest wild population outside Indonesia and Timor-Leste, is giving researchers a rare chance to study the birds' behavior while helping them breed safely. Genetic tests even show these urban cockatoos carry surprisingly rich diversity, a hopeful sign for the species' future.
caption: A little yellow crest, a new home
alt: A watercolor of a yellow-crested cockatoo with a sunny yellow crest and pink cheeks, perched on a park branch next to a wooden nest box where a second cockatoo peeks out; a climbing rope hangs on the tree, Bauhinia flowers bloom in front, and a small flock flies over a soft Hong Kong skyline.

title: Probiotics prevented coral bleaching during a Red Sea heat wave: Study
summary: Scientists gave a patch of Red Sea coral a dose of beneficial bacteria, and when a scorching heat wave hit in 2022, those treated corals stayed vividly healthy while others around them bleached. It's the first real-world proof that coral probiotics can help reefs survive marine heat waves, offering a hopeful new tool as oceans keep warming.
caption: Tiny helpers kept the reef glowing bright
alt: A cheerful, plump round coral character with big eyes and pink cheeks sits on a sunlit Red Sea reef, surrounded by small fish, bubbles, and glowing probiotic specks, while other coral shapes and light rays fill the water around it.

title: Wildlife traffickers are now targeting Indonesia’s critically endangered maleo birds
summary: Maleo birds, found only on the Indonesian island of Sulawesi, bury their eggs in warm volcanic sand instead of sitting on nests, which makes both the birds and their eggs easy targets. Reports now show wildlife traffickers turning their attention to this already critically endangered species, adding a new danger on top of habitat loss. Conservationists are worried this growing illegal trade could push the rare bird even closer to disappearing.
caption: Keeping watch over eggs in the sand
alt: A worried-looking maleo bird with a helmet-shaped head stands over a disturbed sandy nest mound on a dusky volcanic beach in Sulawesi, with faint footprints trailing away and a calm teal sea behind it.

title: Dolphins keep their social and hunting lives in separate waters, study finds
summary: A new study finds that dolphins tend to use their social whistles in one set of waters and switch to quick echolocation clicks when hunting prey in another. Researchers say this separation suggests dolphins organize their daily lives much like we divide work from play, keeping chatty reunions and focused hunts in different parts of their home range. The findings offer a sweet new window into how clever and social these ocean mammals really are.

alt: A cheerful cartoon dolphin leaps through sunlit teal waves, surrounded by tiny fish, bubbles, and a distant whistling pod under a glowing sky.

title: Reintroduced Grauer’s gorilla gives birth in DRC national park, ‘makes us happy’
summary: Lulingu, a Grauer's gorilla once rescued from traffickers and raised at the GRACE sanctuary, was released into Virunga National Park in 2024 and has now given birth to a healthy baby. Caretakers are thrilled, since every birth matters for this critically endangered ape, and the community will soon vote on a name for the newborn. The park still faces conflict and poaching pressures, but this birth is a rare bright spot.
caption: A rescued mama gorilla cradles new hope
alt: A warm watercolor forest scene of a chunky brown mother gorilla with round ears and blush cheeks cradling a smaller baby gorilla against her chest, surrounded by misty green Virunga hills, trees, flowers and distant birds.

title: In war-torn South Sudan, giraffes retain a surprisingly healthy gene pool
summary: Despite decades of war in South Sudan, researchers found that the tiny surviving population of Nubian giraffes is surprisingly genetically diverse and only lightly inbred. Scientists say gene flow across the White Nile has helped keep the population healthy, offering hope that conflict-affected landscapes can still safeguard wildlife. Conservationists now see South Sudan as an unexpected stronghold for this critically endangered giraffe subspecies.
caption: A hopeful giraffe stands tall over healed savanna
alt: A watercolor storybook painting of a spotted Nubian giraffe standing proudly in a golden South Sudan savanna with acacia trees, a winding river, distant giraffes and birds overhead.

title: Fighting to Save the World’s Most Wanted Animal
summary: Across Africa, pangolins are being snared and poached in huge numbers for their keratin scales, prized in illegal wildlife medicine markets. Dedicated caregivers like Lisa Hywood and Julie Vanassche have learned the delicate art of nursing rescued pangolins back to health, walking them through forests each day until they are strong enough to be released back into the wild.
caption: A rescued little scaled one climbs home again
alt: A watercolor storybook scene of a round, scaly orange pangolin walking toward a big forest tree at dusk, with a termite mound, a wooden rescue crate, and a glowing lantern nearby.

title: What Does It Take to Move 2,000 Rhinos?
summary: African Parks bought a struggling South African ranch with 2,000 white rhinos and set out on a decade-long mission to fly and truck them to new protected homes across Africa. The story follows a tense relocation where a sedated calf nearly dies before recovering, showing the risky, hopeful work of keeping the species safe from poachers.
caption: One brave calf, a new savanna home
alt: A warm watercolor savanna at sunset with acacia trees, a transport crate, and a mother rhino standing protectively beside her calf.

title: A Filmmaker on What it Takes to Spend Four Years With Lions
Can This Bone-Eating Bird Be Saved?
summary: In South Africa, Shannon Hoffman runs a breeding program racing to save the critically endangered African bearded vulture. Her team gathers eggs from wild nests in the Drakensberg mountains and raises the chicks with puppet feeding, hoping their offspring can one day be released back into the wild.
